target: Dovrei studiare di più per l'esame.
english: I should study more for the exam.
old: "Dovrei" – conditional of dovere, meaning 'should'.
focus: 'Dovrei' = 'I should' – Italian builds should from the conditional of dovere (must); make that the hook, not a conjugation label.

target: Questo è ciò di cui ho bisogno.
english: This is what I need.
old: 'Cui' follows prepositions: 'la persona di cui parlo' = the person I'm talking about.
focus: 'ciò di cui ho bisogno' – bisogno takes di, so the relative carries it: di cui; use the card's own phrase as the worked example.

target: Mi ero svegliato troppo tardi per la riunione.
english: I had woken up too late to make the meeting.
old: Trapassato prossimo with essere: ero + participio (agrees in gender/number). "Era già partita."
focus: Reflexive 'mi ero svegliato' takes essere and the participle agrees – anchor to this card, cut the off-card sibling example.

target: I colleghi con i quali lavoro sono molto competenti.
english: The colleagues I work with are very competent.
old: "Il quale/la quale" are formal alternatives to "che/cui" – they agree in gender/number and clarify ambiguity.
focus: 'con i quali' – formal alternative to 'con cui' that agrees in gender/number (plural quali here); quote the card's actual form.

target: Quando avrò finito, ti chiamo.
english: When I've finished, I'll call you.
old: Future perfect + future for completed future actions.
focus: 'Quando avrò finito' – future perfect after quando where English says 'when I've finished'; fix the claim, main clause 'ti chiamo' is present.

target: Questo lavoro va fatto subito, non domani.
english: This work must be done right away, not tomorrow.
old: "Andare" + past participle expresses obligation/necessity.
focus: 'va fatto' is literally 'goes done' = must be done – andare + participle as obligation passive; quote va fatto from the card.

target: Non avevano mai assaggiato una pizza così buona.
english: They had never tasted such good pizza.
old: "Non + trapassato + mai" = had never done something. Emphasizes that the action had never occurred before.
focus: 'non ... mai' stacks negatives – literally 'they hadn't never tasted'; the double negative is the trap, not emphasis.

target: Volevo che tu venissi alla mia festa.
english: I wanted you to come to my party.
old: "Venissi" – imperfect subjunctive of venire, after past tense main clause.
focus: Past main clause volevo forces imperfect subjunctive venissi (not venga) – English 'I wanted you to come' hides this; add the hook, quote the card.

target: Ero appena arrivato quando è iniziato a piovere.
english: I had just arrived when it started raining.
old: Trapassato prossimo with essere: ero arrivato.
focus: ero appena arrivato – arrivare takes essere, literally 'I was arrived' where English says 'had'; drop the tense-label lead.

target: Se avessi studiato di più da giovane, ora sarei preparato.
english: If I had studied more when young, I'd now be prepared.
old: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.
focus: Real mixed conditional here: se avessi studiato (past if) pairs with ora sarei (present result) – quote the card, plain words, no textbook label.

target: Bisogna fare attenzione.
english: One must pay attention.
old: 'Bisogna' + infinitive for impersonal necessity.
focus: bisogna never takes a subject – 'one must' is baked into the verb; keep it plain and quote bisogna fare attenzione.

target: Bisogna che tu parta subito.
english: You need to leave right away.
old: Bisogna che requires the subjunctive.
focus: Contrast bisogna + infinitive (general necessity) with bisogna che tu parta + subjunctive (aimed at a specific person).

target: Voglio che tu venga alla festa.
english: I want you to come to the party.
old: Volere che + subjunctive expresses a wish for someone else's action.
focus: English uses an infinitive ('I want you to come'); Italian needs voglio che + venga – anchor with the card's own voglio che tu venga.

target: Venne a sapere la verità troppo tardi.
english: He found out the truth too late.
old: 'Venire a' + infinitive: achievement.
focus: venne a sapere literally 'came to know' = found out – lead with the literal logic, drop the bare 'achievement' label.

target: La porta viene chiusa alle sei di sera.
english: The door is closed at six in the evening.
old: Passive with venire: emphasizes the action happening regularly.
focus: viene chiusa = gets closed (the event happening); essere-passive would read as a state – fix the shaky 'regularly' claim, quote viene chiusa.

target: Se fossi te, lo farei senza pensarci.
english: If I were you, I'd do it without thinking.
old: "Se fossi te" – common Type 2 structure for giving advice.
focus: The se-clause takes fossi, never the conditional – 'se sarei' is the classic English-speaker error; drop the 'Type 2' label.

target: Non riesco a dormire quando fa troppo caldo la notte.
english: I can't sleep when it's too hot at night.
old: "Riuscire a" + infinitive means to manage/succeed in doing something.
focus: non riesco a dormire = 'I can't sleep' – Italian frames inability as not-managing rather than potere; quote the card.

target: Il progetto è da rifare.
english: The project needs redoing.
old: 'Essere da' + infinitive: necessity.
focus: è da rifare = 'is to be redone', it still needs doing – gloss the literal logic and quote the card, drop the bare 'necessity' label.

target: Ho da fare tutto il pomeriggio; ci vediamo stasera.
english: I have things to do all afternoon – see you tonight.
old: "Avere da" + infinitive expresses obligation or things to be done.
focus: Anchor on the card's ho da fare – avere da + infinitive = things you have to do; ho da fare alone also means 'I'm busy'.

target: Questa storia va raccontata per non dimenticare il passato.
english: This story must be told so as not to forget the past.
old: "Andare" + past participle expresses obligation (must be done).
focus: va raccontata = 'must be told' – andare + past participle for obligation; quote va raccontata (tip cites only the infinitive andare, which the card never shows).

target: A meno che non cambi idea, parto domani mattina presto.
english: Unless I change my mind, I'm leaving early tomorrow morning.
old: "A meno che non" (unless) requires subjunctive; the "non" is pleonastic.
focus: The non isn't a negation – a meno che non cambi = 'unless I change'; say dummy non in plain words, keep the subjunctive note.

target: Cerco un hotel che abbia una vista panoramica sul mare.
english: I'm looking for a hotel that has a panoramic sea view.
old: Subjunctive in relative clauses when the antecedent is indefinite or sought.
focus: cerco un hotel che abbia – a hotel you're only hoping exists takes abbia, not ha; plain words, quote the card, no 'antecedent'.

target: Gli ho detto di non preoccuparsi.
english: I told him not to worry.
old: Imperative becomes 'di + infinitive' in reported speech.
focus: True rule, unanchored – quote ho detto di non preoccuparsi: a reported command becomes di + infinitive.

target: Continua a piovere da tre giorni senza interruzione.
english: It has been raining for three days without interruption.
old: "Continuare a" + infinitive expresses ongoing, persistent action.
focus: The gem is piove da tre giorni – present tense + da where English says 'has been raining'; replace the continuare-a gloss with that.

target: Saranno le tre del pomeriggio; il sole è ancora alto.
english: It must be about three in the afternoon – the sun is still high.
old: Simple future of probability: "saranno" = they must be (conjecture).
focus: saranno le tre = 'it must be about three' – future tense used for a guess, not future time; drop the textbook label and the off gloss 'they must be'.

target: Quindi, è inutile continuare a discutere.
english: So, it's pointless to keep arguing.
old: Verb + a/di + infinitive: continuare a (continue to), smettere di (stop), cominciare a (begin to). The preposition is fixed.
focus: Keep the fixed-preposition rule anchored on continuare a discutere; cut from two sibling examples to one.

target: Mi sono fatto aiutare da un esperto.
english: I got help from an expert.
old: 'Farsi' + infinitive: having something done for oneself.
focus: mi sono fatto aiutare = 'I got someone to help me' – farsi + infinitive means having it done for you; quote the card (tip cites only farsi, which never appears).

target: Si è messo a ridere senza alcun motivo apparente.
english: He started laughing for no apparent reason.
old: "Mettersi a" + infinitive means to start doing something, often suddenly.
focus: Anchor the card's own form 'si è messo a ridere' – mettersi a = literally 'put yourself to it', a sudden start; add hook and card quote.

target: Cerco di capire il tuo punto di vista sulla questione.
english: I'm trying to understand your point of view on the matter.
old: "Cercare di" + infinitive means to try to do something.
focus: Lead with the flip: cercare alone = look for, cercare di + infinitive = try to – quote 'Cerco di capire'.

target: Sebbene il viaggio sia stato lungo, ne è valsa la pena.
english: Although the trip was long, it was worth it.
old: "Sebbene" + subjunctive – 'although'.
focus: Sebbene takes subjunctive even for real facts – 'sebbene sia stato lungo' reports something that actually happened; add that angle, drop the bare formula.

target: Mi ha rimproverato di non averla avvisata del cambiamento di programma.
english: She reproached me for not having informed her of the schedule change.
old: "Rimproverare di" + infinitive for reported reproach.
focus: English says 'reproached me FOR not having...', Italian uses di + past infinitive – quote 'di non averla avvisata'.

target: Ha detto: 'Qui si mangia bene.' Ha detto che li si mangiava bene.
english: She said: 'The food is good here.' She said the food was good there.
old: Space shifts: qui → li/la, questo → quello.
focus: Fix accents in the tip (qui → lì/là, questo → quello) and keep it anchored to this card's qui → li shift.

target: Queste regole vanno rispettate da tutti senza alcuna eccezione.
english: These rules must be respected by everyone without any exception.
old: "Andare" + past participle = dovere essere + past participle (must be).
focus: 'Vanno rispettate' = must be respected – andare + past participle carries obligation; quote the card and drop the 'dovere essere' formula phrasing.

target: Sto per partire.
english: I'm about to leave.
old: 'Stare per' + infinitive: imminent action.
focus: First encounter of stare per: 'Sto per partire' = I'm about to leave – on the verge of; give it a hook and the card quote instead of a fragment.

target: Si è lasciato convincere.
english: He let himself be convinced.
old: 'Lasciarsi' + infinitive: allowing something to happen to oneself.
focus: 'Si è lasciato convincere' uses an ACTIVE infinitive where English needs 'be convinced' – lasciarsi + infinitive = let it happen to you; make that the hook.

target: Sono andato a trovare i miei genitori nel fine settimana.
english: I went to visit my parents over the weekend.
old: "Andare a" + infinitive indicates motion with purpose.
focus: 'Andare a trovare' = go VISIT someone, not 'go find' – lead with the trovare flip and quote 'Sono andato a trovare'.

target: L'ho già letto, questo libro; non serve comprarlo di nuovo.
english: I've already read it, this book – no need to buy it again.
old: Right dislocation: topic placed after the main clause for afterthought.
focus: Drop 'right dislocation' – plain words: pronoun first, noun tagged on after as an afterthought; quote 'L'ho già letto, questo libro'.

target: Andavano dicendo che era un genio.
english: They kept saying he was a genius.
old: 'Andare' + gerundio: gradual/repeated action.
focus: 'Andavano dicendo' = they went around saying – andare + gerund for ongoing/repeated action; quote the card and use plain words, not 'gerundio'.

target: Hanno da fare tutto il giorno.
english: They have things to do all day.
old: 'Avere da' + infinitive: having to do.
focus: 'Hanno da fare' = they're busy / have things to do – avere da + infinitive; anchor the idiom, note it is not English 'have to do' obligation.

target: Abbiamo molto da imparare dalla cultura di questo paese.
english: We have much to learn from this country's culture.
old: "Avere da" can imply both obligation and opportunity.
focus: Anchor 'molto da imparare' – avere + noun + da + infinitive here reads as opportunity, not obligation; quote the card.

target: Ha chiesto che tutti fossero presenti alla riunione straordinaria.
english: He asked that everyone be present at the extraordinary meeting.
old: "Ha chiesto che" + subjunctive for polite/formal reported commands.
focus: The real driver is the different subject: chiedere che + subjunctive when you name who must act ('che tutti fossero presenti') vs chiedere di + infinitive; drop 'polite/formal'.

target: Mi sono messo a studiare seriamente solo a metà semestre.
english: I started studying seriously only halfway through the semester.
old: "Mettersi a" emphasizes the beginning of an action, often with effort or resolve.
focus: Second angle on mettersi a: effort/resolve – anchor with the card's 'mi sono messo a studiare seriamente'.

target: Può darsi che il museo sia chiuso il lunedì mattina.
english: It may be that the museum is closed on Monday mornings.
old: "Puo darsi che" (it may be that) triggers subjunctive.
focus: Fix the accent (può) and add the literal hook: può darsi = roughly 'it can give itself' = maybe; può darsi che + subjunctive, quote the card.

target: È necessario che tutti partecipino alla riunione di domani.
english: It is necessary that everyone participates in tomorrow's meeting.
old: Impersonal expressions of necessity trigger subjunctive.
focus: Anchor this card: 'È necessario che...partecipino' – impersonal è + adjective + che triggers subjunctive; quote the card instead of the generic rule.

target: Sosteneva che fosse impossibile.
english: He claimed it was impossible.
old: 'Sostenere che' + subjunctive in reported speech.
focus: 'Sosteneva che fosse impossibile' – the subjunctive marks the reporter's distance from the claim; make that the hook, quote 'fosse'.

target: Ha detto che era stanco.
english: He said he was tired.
old: Reported speech: present becomes imperfect.
focus: Anchor the card: direct 'Sono stanco' → reported 'era stanco' – present backshifts to imperfect; add the card quote.
